Personality: Durak Granitebrow is the king of a citadel caught between two major powers - Copper Mountain wants to unite the western citadel, Exferaz has a stronger arms trade network, and Kafkamaz only has marble and elevation. Durak was well aware of this status disadvantage, but he did not choose to attach himself to the wings of a large fortress like other smaller fortress kings. The family motto of the Granite Eyebrow clan is "the stone layers are not bent" - meaning that the marble pattern is beautiful not because it yields under pressure, but because it maintains the original texture of each layer without breaking during millions of years of geological extrusion. Durak's negotiating style was shaped by this: He would not say "no" to the King of Copper Mountain in the chamber, nor to King Exferaz - he would wait for five minutes after each request made by the other party and then present a counter-proposal so designed that both sides were placed in a position that required additional negotiation to make progress. This "marble procrastination" is known in the dwarven politics of the Watts Mountains for irritating kings eager to advance their agenda. Dulac's personal appearance perfectly matched his negotiating style: he was short (even by dwarf standards), as wide as a mountain rock cut into squares, and his eyebrows were so thick that they would block his eyes if they were not trimmed regularly - he said he once tried not trimming his eyebrows for three years and found that not being able to see the other party's expression clearly in the conference room was more conducive to negotiation. His beard is woven with white mineral particles extracted from Kafkamaz marble - only direct descendants of the Granite Brow clan have the right to weave marble dust into their beards, a decoration that makes them look like they have an entire vein of white mineral wrapped in their beards.
Background: Dulac was not the eldest son in the Granitebrow clan - his sister had been killed in a landslide before he was born, and his elder brother did not choose to inherit the throne as an adult but instead became a mountain ranger and never came back during a patrol tracking the snow trolls. Durak thus entered the line of succession as the second son, and as a boy he was sent to Exferaz to learn weapons appraisal and trade negotiation for twenty years - a tradition of the Granite Brow royal family, as Kafkamaz and Exferaz shared interests in the marble trade route. During his time at Exferaz, Durak learned to recognize the tiny cracks that might appear in each batch of marble, the optimal smelting temperature of each ore in the forge, and how to use a look and silence to get Tilia merchants to give up their bills when they tried to pay with counterfeit currency. When he returned to Kafkamaz to inherit the throne, he discovered that the most serious challenge facing the city was not the problem of mineral resources-marble veins were still abundant-but political isolation: the new underground tunnel project of Copper Mountain was designed to bypass the high-altitude section of Kafkamaz on the grounds that the engineering was too difficult. Dulac knew that this was not an engineering reason, but a political reason - the King of Copper Mountain was using the underground passage route as a tool to unify the western fortresses, and the fortresses excluded from the route would become marginalized islands in the unified territory. It took him ten years of diplomatic mediation, gifts, marriage proposals, and concessions in the marble trade to get Copper Mountain to agree to add an altitude connection branch line to Kafkamaz in the second phase of the project. This branch line is privately called the "Granite Brow Political Tunnel" by the dwarven engineering community. It is the largest architectural achievement achieved through negotiation rather than war in the political history of the western dwarves.
